newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Societe Generale Asia income grows 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: Societe Generale Asia income grows 30 pct.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale said on Wednesday its Asia-Pacific income grew 30.3 percent in 1996 to 632 million francs, from 485 million in 1995.
The bank said in a statement Asia represented 16.5 percent of Socgen International and Finance's gross operating income.

It quoted Socgen's chief executive officer, Daniel Bouton, as saying the bank aimed to become a top investment bank in Asia through its network and its twin banking vehicles: Socgen Asia for the debt and capital markets and Socgen Crosby for equities.

It said the bank's product focus was on loans, trade finance, project finance, loans syndication, capital market issues such as floating rate notes, fixed income such as bonds and regional and main currencies, private placements and equity issues.
